sources.name: C++ Core Guidelines: concurrency and shared state
extracted_methods: identify shared mutable state
trace synchronization and callback context
inspect cancellation, shutdown, and destruction races
trigger_evidence: mutex, atomic, condition variable, callback, future, thread, coroutine
shared state read and write paths
prohibited_generalizations: Do not infer a race from a symbol name alone
Do not prescribe a particular lock or memory-order change
Do not emit unit-level concurrency tests

sources.name: C++ Core Guidelines: resource ownership and lifetime
extracted_methods: build acquire-transfer-release chains
compare normal and error cleanup paths
distinguish ownership from borrowing at C/C++ boundaries
trigger_evidence: alloc, free, release, destroy, close, refcount, RAII
partial initialization or error exit
prohibited_generalizations: Do not assume every allocation is dynamic physical memory
Do not label an imbalance a leak without a reachable path
Do not generate replacement stubs or mocks

sources.name: DPDK performance and queueing guidance
extracted_methods: separate throughput, latency, and control-plane rate
record queue depth, burst, worker, affinity, and version conditions
verify recovery after pressure removal
trigger_evidence: rte_, PMD, mbuf, ring, lcore, queue depth, burst
throughput, latency, drop, retry, backpressure
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat DPDK microbenchmark results as end-to-end storage performance
Do not assume DPDK is present from a generic queue symbol
Do not infer a regression without a baseline or specification

sources.name: Chaos Mesh resilience experiment methodology
extracted_methods: define steady state before fault injection
bound blast radius and recovery expectation
verify service recovery after fault removal
trigger_evidence: timeout, retry, reset, reconnect, fault injection, recovery
service interruption or degraded state
prohibited_generalizations: Do not assume a fault-injection interface exists
Do not apply Kubernetes-specific experiments to firmware or drivers
Do not claim resilience from restart-only recovery
